claim: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) only evaluates the per-client resource when one exists, so an 'all clients' permission (bound to the 'Clients' type resource) is ignored for any client that has its own permission, denying access the admin was granted.

init() returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists, so realms initialised before this PR never get the 'Clients' type resource or the new configure/map-roles-client-scope/map-roles-composite scopes, and creating Clients permissions fails there.

getClientsWithPermission() queries resources by type 'Clients', but per-client resources are created without a type, so it can only ever return the literal 'Clients' (the type resource name) and never real client IDs.
getResourceName() has a branch for Users but not for the new Clients type, so GET /policy/{id}/resources returns a null displayName for client resources instead of the clientId / 'All clients'.

With V2 the ClientRemovedEvent listener is now skipped (gated on the V1 feature) and nothing else removes the per-client resource (named by client UUID, owned by the admin-permissions client), so permissions referencing a deleted client stay behind.
body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] No V2 cleanup of per-client resources on client removal

**Severity:** LOW — deleting a client leaves orphaned V2 resource and permissions

### The Problem
The PR wraps the listener in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ))`, which is correct for avoiding `UnsupportedOperationException` from `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, but no V2 replacement is added.

### Theory / Proof
`ClientApplicationSynchronizer` only deletes the removed client's own resource server and cleans `client` policies; it does not look at resources in the admin-permissions resource server. V2 per-client resources are owned by the admin-permissions client, so `findByOwner(clientId)` style cleanup would not find them either.

### What happens today vs. what will break
After deleting a client, its permissions remain listed; with finding 4 fixed, `getResourceName` would throw `ModelIllegalStateException` for the dangling resource when listing that permission's resources.

### Research
V1 handled this via `setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` in this very listener.

### Recommendation
Add a V2 branch that removes the per-client resource (and permissions left with no resources) from the admin-permissions resource server:
```java
} else if (AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.isAdminPermissionsEnabled(realm) && event instanceof ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent cast) {
    AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.removeResourceObject(session, realm, cast.getClient().getId());
}
```
